PullRequest.Title: docs: unwrap Agent Host prose
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Remove manual line wrapping from prose in active Agent Host documentation, directly related SDK packaging and remote-host documentation, and repository skills. Keep each paragraph on one source line so editors and renderers can wrap naturally.

Add a repository instruction discouraging fixed-width Markdown wrapping. Preserve Markdown structure, code, and intentional hard breaks. Leave unrelated documentation, Claude planning/context documents, the Codex README, built-in skills, and test fixtures unchanged.

### Validation

- Markdown rendering-equivalence check using the existing `markdown-it` parser: passed for all 20 reformatted documents, normalizing soft breaks to spaces.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Commit pre-commit hygiene hook: passed.
- Builds and runtime tests were not run; all 21 changed files are Markdown only.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke the sweeper-plan or sweeper-implement repository skills for one issue
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The agent reads the skill, checks repository state, queries GitHub, optionally runs the named tests, and in implement mode waits for maintainer approval before push/PR creation. The diff only joins soft-wrapped prose and does not add a step to this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the sweeper review record and live GitHub issue/PR state with gh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded set of live queries for one issue, repeated once before shipping where already required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same gh commands, gates, ordering, and recheck were present before the prose was unwrapped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These gates must complete before planning, implementation, or shipping proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run git state checks and the existing targeted validation commands named by the issue spec
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Repository checks once per invocation and targeted tests according to the unchanged spec, including the pre-change/post-change validation already required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subprocess work and validation requirements existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Checks and tests block handoff or PR creation as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Push the approved branch and create one draft pull request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one push and one draft PR creation for a successful invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same push and gh pr create operations were already prescribed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the final shipping path after approval, unchanged by the reflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected issue, one review record, one live issue, and the tests named by its spec; effective cardinality and retry rules are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Live gates remain sequential; implementation tests follow the existing spec; SDK/build work described elsewhere remains unchanged. No new parallelism, limiter, queue, or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The skills still fetch live GitHub state rather than relying on a cache, and the optional local plan file remains the same authority. No cache key, positive/negative cache, invalidation, or coalescing behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no performance mechanism changed: the complete skill diffs only replace Markdown soft line breaks with spaces.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent interpretation of formatting can vary, but the commands, counts, ordering, and prose content are unchanged; no concrete extra boundary call or repeated work is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Boundary operations remain the same and no additional work moved onto the workflow critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke the setup-environment skill to inspect local tool availability
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The agent checks tool versions, searches expected install locations for non-PATH tools, retries one alternate location, and reports missing tools. The reflow collapses the nested textual numbering onto one source line but adds no command or loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute version checks for tools available on PATH
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One version check per required PATH tool, with the unchanged instruction to group checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical tool-version checks were required before the line reflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The checks must complete before the environment summary is produced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search expected and alternate installation locations for each non-PATH tool
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two searches per non-PATH tool under the unchanged prose.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two-attempt search procedure existed as a nested list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Search completion determines whether each tool is reported missing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The configured set of required tools; each non-PATH tool still has at most two described location searches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PATH version checks may still be grouped as previously instructed; non-PATH searches retain the same bounded retry count. No concurrency policy changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is specified before or after the diff; checks inspect the current environment each invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the textual operation count remains bounded and unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A model could parse flattened numbering differently, but that would be an instruction-format correctness concern; there is no high-confidence evidence of extra searches or unbounded work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The diff does not establish additional filesystem or subprocess work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or render the changed Markdown documentation and architecture references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An editor or Markdown renderer reads and parses the selected document, then lays out the same prose. Agent Host startup, chat listing, telemetry export, SDK packaging, and remote connection flows are only described by these files and are not executed by them.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected Markdown file whose character content is nearly unchanged; paragraph count and semantic content remain effectively the same.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer behavior and repository documentation loading are unchanged; no runtime queue, worker, or connection concurrency is configured by the edits.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Editor/GitHub document caches are external to these files. No cache key, invalidation rule, runtime cache, or negative-cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because all architecture, telemetry, SDK, test, and remote-host changes are Markdown-only prose reflow and do not alter executable configuration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact Markdown tokenization can differ slightly when soft breaks become spaces, but file sizes and parse complexity remain linear and comparable, with no plausible user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Runtime startup, database, filesystem, subprocess, IPC, and network behavior described in these documents is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 21 changed files and every paginated diff hunk. The PR contains Markdown prose reflow plus a Markdown authoring instruction; it introduces no executable performance mechanism, expensive-boundary fan-out, retained state, cache change, concurrency burst, or critical-path work. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
